analysis:
Examined DaemonStateFile.swift base/head. The head adds three optional diagnostic fields to DaemonState: enabledModelsAtStart and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch (head 54-61) and selectedModelRecovery (head 68-70). It also adds the matching init parameters and assignments (head 374-378, 413-417). The fields are Optional, so older state files still decode, and schema stays 1. They hold model IDs, timestamps and blocker strings. Model identity is already public through heartbeats, so this adds no prompt, key or token exposure (A-001, A-003, A-008). The write/read path (head 658-677) is unchanged: atomic write, best-effort, and the existing DARKBLOOM_STATE_FILE override. The doc comments describe the file as read-only diagnostics, and lifecycle commands use a separate owner-only mailbox, so these fields do not create a control channel.

The added file SelectedModelRecovery.swift (unit 81f267b051da25ee:0) came with metadata only. It was visible solely through the truncated patch excerpt: a recovery queue with backoff of 30s to 600s, a 120s minimum idle time before a victim is evicted, and a 15s pause recheck. Its full source and its integration (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery: eviction of unselected idle models, load attempts) were not supplied.

Questions for integration:
- Recovery loads must still respect the TB-012/T-059 add-on hold model-load fence.
- Recovery-driven loads and evictions must not interfere with in-flight requests or local-request exclusions (T-010, T-029, A-018).
- Shutdown must cancel the attempt task.
- Blocker strings written to the state file must not contain sensitive content.

No regression was identified in the supplied lines. Missing source for the recovery logic is a coverage limit, not evidence that it is safe.
